attributes.scope: MWCC GC 1.2.5 family, and any lane reading a `stmw rN` / frame-size delta out of `fndiff --ops` IMMEDIATE rows or probe.py's slot map. Concerns the INFERENCE from a save-set delta to a named value, not the delta itself.

falsifier: Exhibit a function whose `stmw` save-set delta IS attributable to the residual family a diff-cluster reading assigns it to, confirmed by a defs census showing the surplus register carries that family's value and no other -- that would show the inference from residual family to register identity is sometimes sound and this law over-warns. Conversely, re-run the defs census on do_players after the cached-web clusters close: if the save set moves to r16 at that moment, the web and the save-set delta were coupled after all, and only the ROUTE to the conclusion was wrong rather than the conclusion.
subject: project:gdl
value: A SAVE-SET DELTA TELLS YOU HOW MANY CALLEE-SAVED REGISTERS EACH SIDE USED. IT DOES NOT TELL YOU WHICH VALUE THE SURPLUS ONE HOLDS, AND THE RESIDUAL'S LOUDEST FAMILY IS NOT EVIDENCE FOR THAT. The cheap defs census -- count writes to r14..r31 in both streams and read the ADDR16_LO materialisations -- costs no build and answers it directly; a diff-cluster reading of the same delta guessed wrong here and was carried across two runs as a mandatory lever. MEASURED: do_players reads `stmw r15,140(r1)` frame 264 against the target's `stmw r16,136(r1)` frame 256, and a prior record concluded that the extra register WAS the cached potionicon_tab+0xC40 web because that web dominated the visible clusters. The defs census refutes it. Our r15 is a .rodata base, materialised `addi r15,r4,0 @...rodata.0` at +0x28 and spent on five message-box string pointers at displacements 112/124/136/152/164 before being recycled as a loop counter -- and THE TARGET DEDICATES A CALLEE-SAVED REGISTER TO EXACTLY THE SAME VALUE, `addi r17,r4,0 @lbl_80113AE0` at +0x28 with its own five strings at 996/1008/1020/1036/1048. Both streams also cache the same seven ADDR16_LO bases in total. The cached +0xC40 web lives in r18 (the walked loop pointer, advanced `addi r18,r18,13148`) and r20, neither of which is the boundary register the save set names. THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE, and the reason this is worth a law: the prescribed cure that followed from the misidentification -- shrink the declared-local set so the allocator has no spare register -- was measured DEAD in both available directions. Scoping the only legally scopeable long-lived local REGRESSED real 1154 -> 1182 while the prologue still read `stmw r15,140(r1)` frame 264, which was the prior record's OWN stated refutation condition; block-scoping and renaming a walked loop pointer came back BYTE-IDENTICAL, the edit folding away before codegen. PROCEDURE: on any save-set or frame delta, run the defs census FIRST and name the surplus register's value from its own definition site, THEN pick the axis. Corollary of the guards-are-measurements discipline: a save-set delta is a measurement of the ALLOCATOR'S BUDGET, not an index into the residual you happen to be reading.
